simple.meaning: פְּלֵתִי (Pᵉlêthîy) appears 7 times in the Hebrew Scriptures and is introduced as a son in the family line and in connection with kingship and in connection with priesthood and in connection with prophetic witness.
simple.biblicalBackground: The first appearances are in 2 Samuel, 1 Kings, 1 Chronicles, beginning at 2 Samuel 8:18. BibleIQ detects the main surrounding context as family line, kingship, priesthood, prophetic witness, Israel.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to פְּלֵתִי (H6432) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: People in Scripture are understood by their place in the story. BibleIQ follows פְּלֵתִי through the actual verses so the reader sees the person in context instead of as an isolated dictionary entry.

timeline.evidenceText: Benaiah the son of Jehoiada was over the Cherethites and the Pelethites, and David’s sons were chief ministers.
All his servants passed on beside him; and all the Cherethites, and all the Pelethites, and all the Gittites, six hundred men who came after him from Gath, passed on before the king.
Joab’s men went out after him, and the Cherethites and the Pelethites, and all the mighty men; and they went out of Jerusalem, to pursue Sheba the son of Bichri.
Now Joab was over all the army of Israel, Benaiah the son of Jehoiada was over the Cherethites and over the Pelethites,
So Zadok the priest, Nathan the prophet, Benaiah the son of Jehoiada, and the Cherethites and the Pelethites went down and had Solomon ride on king David’s mule, and brought him to Gihon.
The king has sent with him Zadok the priest, Nathan the prophet, Benaiah the son of Jehoiada, and the Cherethites and the Pelethites; and they have caused him to ride on the king’s mule.
and Benaiah the son of Jehoiada was over the Cherethites and the Pelethites; and the sons of David were chief officials serving the king.
